name: context-tax-audit
for: Inventory everything an agent injects into each request besides the user's message, such as system prompt, environment info, skill list, tool definitions, per-turn context blocks and reminders, and check necessity, frequency, precision, position and prompt-cache impact.
when: Use when reviewing an agent's prompt assembly, chasing low cache hit rates, or trimming per-turn overhead.

name: independent-review
for: Review a code change from a clean context, the way an outside reviewer would.
when: Use after the agent finishes an implementation, before merging, or when asked for an independent or second-opinion review of a diff.

name: long-session-check
for: Check how an agent or a working session handles long conversations, covering tool-result clearing, compaction, what gets written to files, when to start a new session, and how memory is scoped.
when: Use when a long session starts forgetting constraints, after several compactions, or when reviewing an agent's compaction and memory design.

name: subagent-split-check
for: Decide whether a piece of work should go to a subagent or stay in the main agent loop.
when: Use before spawning subagents, when designing a multi-agent architecture, or when auditing an existing set of subagents for merging back.

name: taste-to-checks
for: Turn a review correction we keep making on agent output into something that runs on its own, a test, lint rule, hook, CI step or project rule, so the miss does not come back next session.
when: Use when we keep correcting agents on the same mistake (import order, naming, a forbidden API, a missing test), when the same review comment shows up on a second PR, or after a review finds a miss that a check could have caught.
